findings.reason: the dependency exists only in the queue-ordering meta, so the section as read states no wait and the correction is a one-attribute edit that makes the two declarations consistent.
findings.text: section 15's own declaration reads data-links="" while plan-section-depends-on declares "s15":["codac-uda-signals#s4"], so the two declarations of the same dependency disagree; §6 has the mirror defect at :76 (data-links omits s13, which the meta requires), and a reader of either section sees a wait that is not there

findings.reason: without the exemption the node can complete its measurement correctly and still fail its control on two of the five sources it names, so the control must be narrowed to sources that hold variable names and the remaining sources must record why no pre-registered variable applies.
findings.text: §15's positive control demands "for each source, one variable known beforehand to appear in it is found through the stated access path", but the section's own Delivers list includes the plant breakdown structure in ICP and the naming convention documents, which map component codes and prose rather than containing archive variable names, so no variable can be pre-registered as appearing in them and the control cannot pass for a source that is working; §15 has no clause allowing such a source to record its own outcome, although §9 was given exactly that clause for surfaces with no consumer

findings.reason: an unrecorded follow-up is work the plan promises and does not carry, and the plot guard is already known to exist as a fourth copy awaiting that migration.
findings.text: §7's Delivers states that "moving them onto it is a follow-up, not part of this section", but the Followups block holds a single entry (f-cus-001, "Build the scanner and loader sections") and nothing records the figure-script migration, so the deferred work the section names has no tracked owner; the same text at :158 is also stale, still describing "sections 2 to 9 buildable" while §1, §2, §3, §4, §5, §7 and §9 now carry data-status="done"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — scripts/codac_uda_prototype/ and docs/evidence/fragments/codac-uda-signals/prototype-report.md both resolve in the repository, and the figure directories the landed sections cite exist; extensionless hrefs were resolved as <path>.html before judging.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §15's positive control requires, for each source, "one variable known beforehand to appear in it", but two of the five source types the section names (the plant breakdown structure in ICP, the naming convention documents) hold component codes and prose rather than archive variable names, so the control is unsatisfiable for a source behaving correctly and §15 carries no exemption of the kind §9 was given.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every section puts its measurements in the landing record and its documents under docs/evidence/fragments/codac-uda-signals/, with the figure directory docs/figures/codac-uda-signals/ present; no section writes evidence to a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.

rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the root causes §1 records (no data-system entry in the facility configuration, an executor that applies setup commands only on its remote branch, the schema gaps) are the ones the sections repair; every endpoint named in the changed text is obtainable from the sources it cites and each measure can fail; no section prescribes a code path, a step sequence or a function to call.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each node names one deliverable; §7's save function is the guard for the figures it delivers, not a second goal.
